title: Claude designs more efficient quantum circuits
summary: Claude designed circuits for eight basic operations (chemistry, optimization, physical simulation, and number theory), assessed by an automated verifier. In several cases they outperform the best published circuits; for example, a point addition used 17 times fewer gates at the cost of 12% more qubits. Key identities were checked with simulation and Lean; a memory shortcut in the decoder fails about once in 10,000 times.

evidence.tested: An automated evaluator checked each circuit for correctness and scored qubits times gates; results were compared with published designs, divsteps was checked by simulation and Lean, and decoder memory was measured over 403 million simulated decodings.
evidence.unknown: The decoder memory shortcut fails about once in 10,000 runs; gains apply to individual primitives, not a full fault-tolerant machine; Claude was conservative and needed prompts to broaden its search.
evidence.ai_role: Claude wrote circuits as Python code and revised them in a closed loop with evaluator feedback, with no human input between rounds, and reconstructed branch information to reduce memory.
